It remains the operative check on a v≤11 FULL manifest, whose arrays are an independent committed record.
- **No Python source change at all.** `SRMECH_ERR_BAD_INPUT` (2) is already the `GenomeBoundingError` analogue and `_raise_native_genome` maps every non-OK status to that type, so the fix surfaces through the existing plumbing. It also reaches `genome_window` / `genome_load` / `genome_genes` / `genome_remove` for free — each reads the catalog through `_catalog_data` before dispatching to native.
- **`SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10; `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 19.** The one function added is `static`, and the only exported function whose BODY changed is `srmech_genome_catalog`, whose signature is untouched — no symbol, typedef, or enumerator moves, and no new status enumerator is introduced. **NO tool-count / Rosetta / registry ripple** — no public callable and no `ToolEntry` change, so `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays **509** and the four generated files are untouched. JPL-clean (≤60-line functions, ≥2 asserts each, no goto/malloc/recursion); pedantic build (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`) clean.
- **Docs.** The `srmech_genome_catalog` header block claimed the catalog "never opens turns.bin" when a manifest is present — false for every store written today (the Python docstring was corrected in rc282; this one was not). Corrected, plus the new `BAD_INPUT` condition and, on the census / registry / load blocks, an explicit **NOT YET BOUND (#955)** note rather than silence.
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_genome_catalog_body_bound_rc337.py` (43 tests) drives four corruption vectors chosen so no single mechanism satisfies them all: **A** a label byte (`byte_offset+2`, `(b+1)%4` — the walk is untouched, only a payload byte changed); **B** the tail payload byte (`len(body)-1`, `^=0x01` — no cap, no marker); **C** a region **MERGE** (the second chromosome's marker → `0x00`, which `genome_block_len` ACCEPTS as a legacy v2 turn, folding the block into the previous region so `n_chromosomes` silently drops 2 → 1 — invisible to every per-region check because the tree is re-derived with the wrong number of regions, and caught pre-rc337 by `genome.py:8438` alone); and **D** a control (`byte_offset ^ 0x01` → `0x42`, genuinely unrecognised, already rejected before rc337 on EVERY entry point and unchanged by it — note `(b+1)%4` is NOT a usable control, since `0x43+1 mod 4 == 0` is what vector C shows is accepted). Statuses are pinned PER VECTOR; both projections are asserted by TYPE (never message text); the controls that must still SUCCEED are pinned too — a clean store on the whole surface *including* the `#955` half, a manifest-LESS genome with a corrupt body (nothing committed to bind against — the case an unconditional `memcmp` would have broken), and a manifest-LESS **append**, which is the regression the first cut actually produced. A no-mutation guard proves `genome_remove` / `genome_replace` leave `turns.bin` and `manifest.json` byte-identical when the bound fires. **10 fail against the pre-fix library; 31 pass + 12 `xfail` after.** The C-host smoke `c/test/test_srmech_genome.c` gains a matching block (**205 pass / 1 fail pre-fix → 206 pass / 0 fail after**): every corruption case it had flipped byte 0 — the cap's KIND byte, which the structural walk rejects on its own — so the C had **never** exercised a body that walks perfectly but carries a corrupt payload. It also asserts the census / load non-binding out loud, and that repairing the byte makes the catalog read again.

## [0.9.0rc336]

_**Class N — `best_rational` gains a `with_path` keyword that emits the Stern-Brocot / continued-fraction path it was always computing and discarding: the approximation *holonomy* becomes a first-class output.**_ `best_rational(p, q, max_d)` already walks the CF convergent recurrence (`a_k = ⌊p/q⌋`, `hₖ/kₖ` mediants) and kept only the landing convergent. The sequence of accepted partial quotients `[a_0, a_1, …]` IS the compact continued fraction = the run-length encoding of the Stern-Brocot L/R mediant path to the approximant = the Class-N *holonomy* ("how many times the denominator wraps the numerator" at each level). rc336 emits it on request. Outcome of the 2026-07-25 packed-Q spike (notebook §3.44): of the three framings, path-emission was the one SOLID, near-free find (packed-Q fixnum transport is niche → deferred; the "uniform bignum layer" was an honest null → the tuple + native-bignum `int` uniformity already exists).

- **`best_rational(numerator, denominator, max_denominator, *, with_path=False)`** — keyword-only, default `False` **preserves the pinned `(p', q')` 2-tuple** (`tests/test_rational_parity.py`). `with_path=True` returns `(p', q', path)` where `path` is the CF partial quotients of the accepted convergents; folding `path` back reproduces exactly `(p', q')`, and for `max_denominator ≥ q` it is the FULL continued fraction of `p/q` (equals `continued_fraction(p, q)`). Distinct from `continued_fraction` (which has no denominator budget and whose int64 C peer can't take a bignum coordinate): this is the **`max_d`-bounded** walk with its landing point, and it covers the `> u64` bignum-fallback regime.

- **Additive C — `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10** (a new exported symbol, no existing signature changed). JPL-clean (caller-arena, no malloc/goto/recursion, ≤60-line function, 3 asserts, no `abs`). Pedantic build (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`) clean.
- **NO tool-count / Rosetta / CEIL ripple** — `with_path` is a keyword on the EXISTING `best_rational` op (no new public callable), so `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays **509**, the op's Rosetta bucket stays `c_dispatched`, and `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` stays **0**. `_c_claims.py` regenerates so `best_rational` now claims BOTH `srmech_best_rational` and `srmech_best_rational_path` (the claim gate checks both resolve in the loaded library). `tests/test_rational_parity.py` — reference paths, path↔convergent fold-back, the unbounded-CF agreement, the bignum-fallback path, and the native == pure byte-identical `(p', q', path)` sweep.
- **Generated `c/src/srmech_tool_registry.c` REGENERATED** — a `ToolEntry` edit reaches the C-side registry data table (the `with_path` param row, param count `3u → 4u`, the new summary + returns). Missing it red'd 10 tests across `test_tool_registry_c_rc184.py` + `test_tool_schema_ops_c_rc185.py` (incl. `test_codegen_is_idempotent`, the freshness guard) on the first CI attempt — the four-generated-file ripple gate is `_c_claims` + `_tool_docs` + the C tool registry + the Rosetta ledger, and it is NOT satisfied by a `-k` slice.
- **The C MCP invoke thunk learns the optional param — a FIFTH ripple axis.** `iv_dispatch` passes `entry->param_count` as `argc`, so growing the registry entry to 4 params made `iv_shape_u_to_pair`'s `argc != 3u` guard DECLINE `best_rational` outright (`invoke_tool_c` → `dispatched=False`, silently falling back to pure — red on all 4 matrix cells). The thunk now accepts BOTH arities and, rather than deferring, implements the option: `with_path` absent/false → the pinned `(p', q')` pair; true → the `(p', q', path)` triple via the new `srmech_best_rational_path`, emitted as TUPLE + nested LIST **byte-identical to the pure `serialise_result`** (verified incl. the `[0, 1, [0]]` edge). A non-BOOL carrier in that slot defers. JPL-clean (fixed 128-entry stack path bound = the kernel's own Euclid cap, no malloc). `test_invoke_tool_c_rc188.py` gains 4 `with_path` batch cases so the arity contract is pinned.

## [0.9.0rc331]

_**#948 Thread B — `One.matrix` earns its `make_class → C` dispatch: the 14×14 `G(σ,θ)` operator emits BYTE-IDENTICAL from a bare-C host.**_ `One.matrix()` was the last One leaf still DEFERRING to pure in the make_class object-model engine. It deferred for two local reasons, both now closed:

- **Correctly-rounded rational→double (`srmech_one.c`).** The old `one_bigrat_to_double` was a NAIVE `floor(|num|·2^96/den)` + limb-Horner that rounds at each 2³²-step once the accumulator passes 2⁵³ — ~1 ULP off CPython `int/int` (round-half-even) for ~0.12% of real `cos/sin` cells (so ~0.12% of real `the_one` inputs emitted the WRONG bytes). It is replaced by a **correctly-rounded round-half-to-even** routine: a DYNAMIC shift `s = 54 − (bitlen(|num|) − bitlen(den))` lands the exact quotient at 55 bits (53 mantissa + 2 guard), the divmod remainder is the sticky bit, round-half-even, and the scale is an EXACT power of two via direct IEEE-754 bit assembly — pure integer + `srmech_bigint` ops, **libm-free, deterministic across Linux/macOS/Windows**, BYTE-IDENTICAL to `int(num)/int(den)` at any magnitude. The dynamic shift also closes a **latent domain bug**: the fixed 96-bit shift silently assumed `|value| ≤ 1`, but a large-angle truncated series (e.g. `θ=27`, 24 terms → `cos ≈ 9.5e6`) sits far outside it; the magnitude-safe shift handles it. Only the two `srmech_one_matrix` callers use the helper (`flat`/`scalar` stay exact-rational), and the wire format (196 row-major doubles) is UNCHANGED — only the low bits of the ~0.12% of cells that were wrong become correct.
- **The One field-DICT vtable thunk (`srmech_make_class.c`).** A new `mc_one_matrix` reads `(sigma, theta[num,den], terms)` from the `one` field-DICT (all int64 — the INPUT is not bignum), calls `srmech_one_matrix`, and wraps the 196 doubles in a `SRMECH_MVAL_MAT` carrier via the new `mc_mat` helper (the carrier `srmech_mcp_serialise_result` already emits byte-for-byte with `json.dumps(serialise_native(Mat))` since rc190). The op `srmech.amsc.cascade.one.one_matrix` is registered in the One vtable — the first One thunk that reads the field DICT (modelled on the sed/genome multi-field thunks). The make_class arena floor is raised (65536 → 131072) to budget the `srmech_one_matrix` workspace this thunk carves, so `One.matrix()` DISPATCHES rather than OVERFLOW-defers.

**Additive C — `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10** (no new symbol, no new callback typedef; `SRMECH_MVAL_FLOAT`/`SRMECH_MVAL_MAT` already exist and cross the boundary only as JSON; `srmech_one_matrix`'s signature + wire format unchanged; `mc_mat`/`mc_one_matrix` are internal statics). `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` unchanged. This is the make_class DEFER surface, NOT the Rosetta wire-glue CEIL — `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS`, `_KNOWN_GLUE_GAPS`, `_WHOLE_OP_C_PEER`, and the Rosetta ledger are untouched; registering a make_class VTABLE op is engine-internal dispatch, NOT a module-level `ToolEntry`, so **tool count stays 509**. Pedantic build (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`) clean; the new C helpers are JPL-clean (no goto/malloc/recursion/`abs`, ≥2 asserts, ≤60-line functions, bounded ≤4-iteration normalisation loop). Tests: `test_one_leaf_ops_c_rc195` flips `test_one_matrix_c_within_tol_of_pure` to a BIT-EXACT native-vs-pure assertion (spread of `(σ,θ,terms)` incl. a `|value|>1` case); `test_make_class_engine_c_rc201` drops `"matrix"` from the still-defers list and proves `One.matrix` DISPATCHES with JSON byte-identical to the pure `CatalogClass` emit.

## [0.9.0rc330]

_**#948 Thread A — per-rung CARRIER ARITHMETIC on `CDRegister`: the register's held Cayley–Dickson element earns a read-only surface.**_ The general N-slot register (rc297) is an ADDRESSING object whose slot map is `{slot → (key, sign∈±1)}` — a content NAME + a Class-C sign, magnitude implicit 1. So the Cayley–Dickson element a register HOLDS is the **signed-basis-unit sum** `x = Σ_{i occupied} sign_i·e_i` (coefficients in `{-1, 0, +1}`), and rc330 surfaces the exact-rational carrier arithmetic over it as a **CORE (always-on) read-only surface** — five new `CDRegister` methods, each the method-form of an already-registered, already-C-dispatched `cayley_dickson.cd_*` op (`composition_of_c`, exactly like `couple_working` is the method-form of `cd_couple_working`):

- **`.element()`** → the length-`dim` exact-`Q` tuple `v[i] = Q(sign_i)` at occupied slots, `Q(0)` elsewhere — the accessor the others read. The register's KEY strings are ORTHOGONAL to the carrier reading; only `(index, sign)` enters, via `slots()`.
- **`.norm()`** → a `Q` scalar, delegating to `cd_norm_sq` (`N(x) = Σ xᵢ²`). Since every occupied coeff is `±1`, this equals the occupied-slot count. A norm is a real scalar, not a CD element — so `Q`, not a register.
- **`.conjugate()`** → a `Q`-tuple, delegating to `cd_conjugate` (Class-K imaginary-slot sign-flip, no `abs()`). Uniform with `cd_conjugate`.
- **`.multiply(other)`** → a `Q`-tuple, delegating to `cd_mult` over the two slot-held elements (symmetric register operands, equal `dim`). Returns a **raw `Q`-tuple, NOT a register**: the product of two signed-basis sums is generally NOT signed-basis (`e_i⊕e_j` collisions make `|coeff|>1`), so it cannot round-trip into a coefficient-free slot register.
- **`.add(other)`** → a `Q`-tuple, delegating to `cd_add` (symmetric register operands, equal `dim`).

**Landmines pinned.** (1) At **dim 16** the carrier `.multiply()` is `cd_mult` — a WELL-DEFINED sedenion product that returns the all-zero element on the zero-divisor witness `x=e1+e10, y=e4−e15` (both nonzero, norm 2; `N(x·y)=0` while `N(x)·N(y)=4`) — NEVER `couple_working`, the ≤7 octonion coupler that is Hurwitz-pinned at cap 7 and RAISES on the sedenion's 15 slots. (2) `CDRegister(16, namespace="SEDENION")` stays **bit-faithful** to `SedenionRegister()` on read / slots: the methods add NO per-instance state (pure reads over `slots()`), so the rc297 oracle equivalence is untouched.

**Python-only, `composition_of_c` — NO C source change, `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10, `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` unchanged.** The methods are the method-form of the already-registered `cd_norm_sq` / `cd_conjugate` / `cd_mult` / `cd_add` ops, so they add **NO module-level `ToolEntry` → tool count stays 509**; the non_compute splits, the Rosetta ledger, and `_c_claims.py` are untouched; no new MCP coercer (a register operand is class-surface-only + coverage-exempt, like `sed_*` / `one.*`, and the `sequence` param + `Q` return are already registered). ## [0.9.0rc328]

_**Laplace–Beltrami α-family — LB earns its two C-native Class-L constructors (task #893 / #888 rec (c)).**_ Task #888 scoped whether srmech "has" the Laplace–Beltrami operator; the verdict (`docs/srmech/notes/laplace_beltrami_scoping.md`) was **we HAVE it latently — LB is a *weighting* of the shipped weighted graph Laplacian, not a new Class-L member** — and held one optional exposure (rec (c)) behind a live LB-spectrum-from-mesh use-case. rc328 IS that conductor decision: it ships the two rec-(c) constructors, both **closed-form, C-native, JPL-clean, no `abs()`, byte-parity**.

- **`laplacian.mass_normalized_laplacian(n, edges, weights=None, masses=None, *, kind="symmetric")`** — the α-family / mass-normalized Laplacian. Builds `L = D − W` then normalizes by a diagonal mass `M`: `kind="symmetric"` → `M^(−1/2)(D−W)M^(−1/2)` (real-symmetric, PSD; nullvector `M^(1/2)·𝟙`); `kind="rw"` → `M^(−1)(D−W)` (random-walk; rows sum to 0). `masses` selects the Coifman–Lafon diffusion-maps **α** position: `masses=None` → `M = D` (weighted degree) is the **α=0** connectivity-normalization (recovers `normalized_laplacian` up to the exact-1 diagonal convention); a supplied `masses` (e.g. Voronoi areas) is the **α=1** metric-normalization — the geometrically-faithful **discrete Laplace–Beltrami** spectrum. The one algebraic step is the `M^(−1/2)` sqrt (the Class-N `srmech_rational_sqrt` cascade, NOT libm); `m_i <= 0` → scale 0 (isolated/massless vertex, mirroring `normalized_laplacian` — the `m_i > 0` guard is a Class-K pin-slot on the sqrt/reciprocal domain, never an ALU `abs`).
- **`laplacian.cotangent_weights(triangles, positions)`** — the discrete-LB cotangent edge weights (Pinkall & Polthier 1993). Takes triangle geometry as given **numbers** (positions as DATA — algebra/spectral only, **NOT** CAD mesh-contact / fabrication geometry) and returns `(edges, weights)` ready for `dense_laplacian`: per triangle it emits the three per-corner `½·cot(θ_k)` contributions for the edge opposite vertex `k`, with `cot θ = (u·v)/|u×v|`, `|u×v| = sqrt(|u|²|v|² − (u·v)²)` (Lagrange). **No trig** (no `cos`/`sin`/`atan`) — one algebraic sqrt per corner; the Lagrange cross magnitude is `≥ 0` in 2-D and 3-D alike, so **no `abs`** (the signed area is a Class-K pin-slot the magnitude never needs). `dense_laplacian`'s parallel-edge accumulation sums the two triangles sharing an edge into the standard `w_ij = ½(cot α_ij + cot β_ij)`. Chain `mass_normalized_laplacian(n, *cotangent_weights(tris, pos)-weights, masses=areas)` for the full α=1 LB pipeline.

**Additive C — `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (new plain symbols, no callback typedef).** Two new exported JPL-clean primitives `srmech_graph_mass_normalized_laplacian` (build `L=D−W` via `srmech_graph_dense_laplacian` + a caller-`scale_ws`-workspace diagonal scale — caller-arena, no malloc/static, reentrant on disjoint `ws`; no node cap) and `srmech_graph_cotangent_weights` (3·n_tri per-corner contributions; `dim ∈ {2,3}`), plus the static helpers `lap_cotangent` / `srmech_cotangent_emit_triangle`. Both are byte-identical to the pure-Python cascades (same `srmech_rational_sqrt`); pedantic build (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`) clean. **Both ops are `c_dispatched`** (whole-op C dispatch) → they add NO wire-glue gap (`CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` stays 8) and are NOT in the non_compute split; `_c_claims.py` gains the two symbol claims (unverifiable ceiling unchanged). **Tool count 507 → 509** (`+2` ToolEntry); the generated `_c_claims.py` / `_tool_docs.py` / `srmech_tool_registry.c` / `srmech_carrier_registry.c` are regenerated from source. `srmech.mcp._coercion._PARAM_COERCERS` gains a `list[tuple[int, int, int]]` → identity handler so `cotangent_weights`'s `triangles` param is JSON-coercible / MCP-callable (a nested-list of vertex-index triples, same JSON-native shape as the existing `list[tuple[int, int]]` edge form). `tests/test_lb_alpha_family_rc328.py` — native == forced-pure byte/value parity on path / cycle / weighted / mass-weighted graphs and right / equilateral / 3-D / two-triangle meshes; the PSD / `[0,2]` / `M^(1/2)𝟙` nullvector / row-sum invariants; the cotangent right-triangle (`0, ½, ½`) and equilateral (`½/√3`) closed forms; the full α=1 LB pipeline; degenerate-triangle + input validation; registration + the c_claims manifest.

## [0.9.0rc326]

_**§𝕆-TURN — octonion DATA turns persist ON DISK: the 𝕆 rung goes end-to-end.**_ The h-genome is a **fibrated Hurwitz tower** (ℝ/ℂ/ℍ/𝕆). rc324 added the 𝕆 CARRIER (`ELEMENT_TYPE_OCTONION`, the 4-bit codec) and rc325 the 𝕆 fiber CHANNEL (holonomy + associator + the `0x4F` cap) — but BOTH deferred **on-disk octonion turn persistence**: `_disk_block` packed only klein4 / Q₈ turns, so a genome FILE could hold the octonion fiber cap but NOT octonion DATA turns. rc326 closes that gap — the exact third stage the Q₈ path took (carrier rc310 → channel rc311 → **on-disk rc312**), ONE Cayley–Dickson rung up. After rc326 the 𝕆 rung is **end-to-end**: octonion turns — INCLUDING the non-quaternionic indices e₄..e₇ the Q₈ 3-bit symbol can never carry — persist to `turns.bin` and round-trip through a genome file.

**`GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` 18 → 19; `OCTONION_PACKED_TURN_MARKER = 0x39` ('9').** The on-disk wire gains a THIRD data-turn packing: an octonion (`ELEMENT_TYPE_OCTONION`) DATA turn **4-bit-packs** under `0x39` (MSB-first contiguous, `ceil(leaf_dim*4/8)` = `ceil(leaf_dim/2)` payload — two nibbles per byte) where the Q₈ turn 3-bit-packs (`0x38`) and the klein4 turn 2-bit-packs (`0x51`); the manifest `carrier` field gains the `"octonion"` value. The marker keys the codec, so a MIXED (klein4 + Q₈ + octonion) walk stays self-describing — v2..v18 bodies read UNCHANGED and klein4 / Q₈ on-disk turns are **BYTE-IDENTICAL** to v18 (only a genome that actually WRITES a `0x39` turn needs the higher version to gate readability). `genome_save(strand, path, coupling, element_type=ELEMENT_TYPE_OCTONION)` threads the octonion packer through the five body walkers (`_walk_region_blocks`, `_stream_body_blocks`, the `genome_load` streamer, `_walk_region_prefix_blocks`, and `_carrier_name_from_body`); a load is self-describing (the body's first packed turn's marker decides the carrier). **The octonion fiber cap now persists too:** `OCT_FIBER_CAP_MARKER` (0x4F) joins `_block_is_cap` (it was already in the read-side `_LEAF_WIDE_BLOCK_MARKERS` and the C `genome_cap_kind` classifier), so an octonion-fiber-bearing strand round-trips through a file — the Python/C cap-classifier asymmetry is closed.

**Additive C — `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (new INTEGER symbols, no callback typedef; the on-disk format is DATA, not a C-wire change).** Two new exported JPL-clean primitives `srmech_genome_octonion_pack_turn` / `srmech_genome_octonion_unpack_turn` (the genome-fully-in-C mirror of the Python 4-bit codec, byte-parity-verified over odd/partial leaf_dims), plus the octonion branches in the C disk walkers: `genome_block_len` + `sc_block_len` classify the `0x39` block width, `genome_scan_fold_block` flags the `"octonion"` carrier, `genome_build_data` emits it (byte-identically to `json.dumps`), `genome_append_head` preserves it across an O(1) append, and `sc_uncouple` decodes an octonion turn (a new static `genome_octonion_uncouple` using `srmech_oct_mult` / `srmech_oct_conjugate`, the Moufang-loop inverse). The C rule pre-images `genome_persistence/v19` + `genome_chromosome/v19` track the bump; pedantic build (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`) clean. **This is PURE disk-wiring — NO new public callable** (mirroring the rc322/rc325 format bumps, not rc312's `upgrade_v15_to_v16` re-interpretation migration: an octonion turn is a distinct 4-bit codec, not a re-read of an existing klein4 turn), so **tool count stays 507** and the non_compute splits are untouched; only the genome-format `== 18` pins bump to `== 19` across the suite. `tests/test_octonion_persistence_rc326.py` — P1 octonion turn disk round-trip (e₄..e₇ present, exact recall, 0x39-only body); P2 the associator survives the disk round-trip (nonzero defect preserved); P3 backward-compat (klein4 + Q₈ + rc325 octonion-fiber-cap strands open + round-trip unchanged; the read-guard accepts old versions); P4 Python↔C byte-identical `turns.bin` + `manifest.json` + the C-codec byte-parity gate; P5 the 𝕆 rung end-to-end (turns AND fiber on disk).

## [0.9.0rc325]

_**§𝕆-FIBER — the octonion FIBER CHANNEL on the genome: the fiber that READS the non-associativity lost at ℍ→𝕆.**_ The h-genome is a **fibrated Hurwitz tower** (ℝ/ℂ/ℍ/𝕆). rc322 gave the genome its ℍ (Q₈) fiber channel (the ordered non-abelian holonomy the winding-invariant per-turn store cannot carry); rc324 added the 𝕆 CARRIER (`ELEMENT_TYPE_OCTONION`, `srmech.amsc.octonion`, `oct_mult`, `OCTONION_SECTORS = 16`). rc325 completes the 𝕆 rung: the **fiber channel that folds a strand of octonion turns and reads the non-associativity** — the exact 𝕆 analog of rc322's ℍ fiber channel, ONE Cayley–Dickson rung up.

**Four new ops (mirroring rc322's three + the new associator).** `genome_octonion_holonomy(turns, leaf_dim=None)` — the ORDERED LEFT-fold octonion product along the strand (`acc[s] = oct_mult(acc[s], turn_t[s])`, identity `+e₀`), **REUSING the rc324 `oct_mult` / `srmech_oct_mult`** (not a reimplemented product); because 𝕆 is non-commutative AND non-associative, a reorder CHANGES the fold. Dispatches to a new whole-op C peer `srmech_genome_octonion_holonomy` (a byte-for-byte mirror of `srmech_genome_fiber_holonomy` with `srmech_q8_mult`→`srmech_oct_mult`; `c_dispatched`, pure `oct_bind` fallback). `genome_octonion_associator(turns, leaf_dim=None)` — the per-slot **non-associativity defect** Q₈ (associative) cannot express: the fully-**LEFT**-associated fold `L[s]` vs the fully-**RIGHT**-associated fold `R[s]` of the same ordered turns; because the octonion index lane is ⊕-associative, `L` and `R` share the index and differ ONLY in the center sign, so `defect[s] = (L[s]>>3) ^ (R[s]>>3) ∈ {0,1}` — identically 0 for `n<3` and any all-quaternionic strand (indices ⊆ `{0,1,2,3}`), nonzero exactly when the turns break associativity (the 𝕆 analog of rc322's `lk_mod2`; a COMPOSED `non_compute` op computed from two folds). `genome_add_octonion_fiber(strand, *, label="octonion")` / `genome_read_octonion_fiber(strand)` — mirror `genome_add_fiber`/`genome_read_fiber`: `add` folds the strand's octonion DATA turns and packs ONE cap; `read` re-derives from the base and returns `{label, holonomy, recomputed, consistent, associator_defect}`.

**`OCT_FIBER_CAP_MARKER = 0x4F` ('O'); `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` 17 → 18.** The new cap is the 𝕆 analog of the v17 `0x46` Q₈ fiber cap — an INTERIOR cap (`genome_cap_kind` recognises it; every cap-skip / codon / data-turn walk flattens past it), holding the LEFT-fold holonomy **4-bit packed** (a dedicated `_pack_oct_fiber_cap`/`_unpack_oct_fiber_cap` pair over the octonion codec — NOT the 3-bit Q₈ packing). A body with NO `0x4F` cap is BYTE-IDENTICAL to v17 (only the manifest `format_version` moves); v2..v17 bodies read UNCHANGED. The C rule pre-images `genome_persistence/v18` + `genome_chromosome/v18` track the bump. A strand may carry BOTH a `0x46` (ℍ) and a `0x4F` (𝕆) cap independently.

**Additive C — `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (new INTEGER symbol, no callback typedef).** `srmech_genome_octonion_holonomy` is a JPL-clean ≤60-line function (≥2 asserts, no goto/malloc/recursion) that reuses `srmech_oct_mult`; pedantic build (`-Werror -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`) clean. Four new `ToolEntry`s (holonomy `c_dispatched`; associator `non_compute`; add/read `composes_c`) — tool count 503 → **507**; the tool registry (`srmech_tool_registry.c`), carrier registry (`srmech_carrier_registry.c`), `_tool_docs.py`, and `_c_claims.py` regenerated; four rosetta rows added; the `== 503` count pins and the `== 17` genome-format pins bumped across the suite. `tests/test_genome_octonion_fiber_rc325.py` — F1 order-carried; F2 non-associativity captured (the defect bit DERIVED from `cd_mult`, convention-robust) + all-quaternionic triple clear; F2b gauge reconstructs; F3 base untouched + both-caps round-trip + pre-rc325 opens; F4 native == pure on ≥200 strands + monkeypatch (numpy-free).

## [0.9.0rc324]

_**§𝕆 — the octonion rung of the fibrated Hurwitz tower: `ELEMENT_TYPE_OCTONION`, a first-class genome carrier one Cayley–Dickson step above Q₈.**_ The h-genome is a fibrated Hurwitz tower (ℝ/ℂ/ℍ/𝕆, recursive-Hopf-nested); rc311 gave the genome its ℍ rung (the Q₈ carrier), and rc324 adds the **𝕆 rung** so a strand can natively STORE octonion-valued data-turns. New pure-Python module `srmech.amsc.octonion` — the DISCRETE octonion Moufang loop `{±e₀, …, ±e₇}` as **4-bit bytes** `o = (sign_bit << 3) | index` (`index = o & 7` the basis unit `e₀..e₇`, `sign_bit = o >> 3` the center `±1`), so `0=+e₀(=+1) … 7=+e₇, 8=−e₀(=−1) … 15=−e₇` — the FULL octonion, including the **non-quaternionic units `e₄..e₇`** the Q₈ sub-block `0..3` cannot reach. Three carrier ops, each with a same-rc byte-exact C peer: `oct_mult` (the loop product; the sign is the Cayley–Dickson cocycle at `dim=8` — computed by the SAME `cd_basis_product` generator Q₈'s `F` is the dim-4 restriction of — xored with the two center bits, **never an `abs()`**), `oct_conjugate` (the loop inverse `conj(e_i)=−e_i` for `i≠0`; `oct_mult(a, oct_conjugate(a))==0`), and `oct_bind` (the elementwise buffer form). `oct_mult` is verified against BOTH `cd_basis_product(8,·,·)` and the exact-rational full-vector `cd_mult` on all 256 basis-unit pairs — the byte object IS the real octonion algebra.

**The genome coupling (`ELEMENT_TYPE_OCTONION = 2`).** `quad_turn(turn, one, element_type=octonion)` RIGHT-couples `stored[i] = oct_mult(turn[i], one[i])`; `recall` / `genes` / `recover_diploid` decouple with the Class-C conjugate `oct_mult(stored[i], conj(one[i]))`. Octonions are globally NON-associative, but each slot holds ONE signed basis unit and the Moufang loop has the **inverse property** `(x·y)·y⁻¹ = x` (`⟨turn, one⟩` is an associative subalgebra by Artin), so the right-conjugate decouple round-trips **byte-exact** — proven on ≥200 random strands INCLUDING indices `4..7`. Like Q₈, the couple SIDE is a HARD runtime assertion (`_oct_side_ok`): 𝕆 is non-commutative, so a wrong-side couple would corrupt silently — the assert pins couple↔uncouple on the same (right) side. Data turns are `sectors=16` (`OCTONION_SECTORS = 16`, a distinct name — `OCT` remains the Q₈ order 8). The associator / fiber-holonomy channel that READS the non-associativity is a LATER rc; rc324 is the carrier that HOLDS the turns.

**The 4-bit turn codec (`_pack_turn_block_octonion`).** An octonion turn packs 4 bits/symbol (`ceil(leaf_dim·4/8)` payload bytes) under a new `OCTONION_PACKED_TURN_MARKER = 0x39` ('9', adjacent to Q₈'s '8'), MSB-first contiguous with canonical zero low-pad — the same layout as the 3-bit Q₈ codec, one bit wider. **Following the rc311→rc312 split precedent, this rc is the CARRIER: the codec is a standalone, directly round-trip-tested function; wiring it into the on-disk region walk (and the `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` bump) is a later rc.** `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` therefore stays **17** — a header-less body still defaults to klein4, and every pre-rc324 klein4/Q₈ strand encodes/decodes/round-trips byte-identically (the size-agnostic element-type discipline; verified as backward-compat).

**Additive C — `SRMECH_ABI_VERSION` stays 10 (new INTEGER symbols, no callback typedef).** New TU `c/src/srmech_octonion_carrier.c` (distinct from the float ODFT `srmech_octonion.c`): `srmech_oct_mult` / `srmech_oct_conjugate` / `srmech_oct_bind`, mirroring `srmech_q8.c` one rung up but calling the iterative `srmech_cd_basis_product(8,·,·)` per pair (no hand-entered 64-entry table to drift; no recursion — JPL Rule 1). Because Q₈ is non-abelian (`i·j = +k` but `j·i = −k`), REORDER CHANGES the fold — the accumulated holonomy IS the gauge = the accumulated `Lk` (biology's supercoiling channel, `Lk = Tw + Wr` accumulating along DNA). The per-slot center-sign `holonomy[s] >> 2` is the accumulated `Lk` mod 2, and it reconstructs `Tw + Wr` exactly (verified against `cwf_consistency_mod2`: the ordered fold of `[i,i,1,1]` → `−1` → `Lk ≡ 1 = (Tw 0 + Wr 1)`; `[−i,i,1,1]` → `+1` → `Lk ≡ 0 = (Tw 1 + Wr 1)`). ## [0.9.0rc320]

_**Class-N precision-contract migration — WAVE 2 (FINAL).** The seven Q61 float-projection ops — `rational.cos` / `sin` / `tan` / `atan` / `atan2` / `exp` / `log` — trade their **DEAD `terms` keyword** (the body never used it; the Q61 cascade has fixed internal caps) for a **LIVE `precision`**. (`cexp` / `complex_exp` thread `precision` through to the underlying trig before the `complex()` display collapse.)_

**`precision=None` (default) → the EXISTING Q61 fast path, BYTE-IDENTICAL to every prior rc.** Every Q61 cascade line is untouched; only the keyword name changed and a `None`-branch selects the Q61 path. The load-bearing **G1 bit-identity gate** (`test_classn_precision_wave2_rc320.py`) asserts `op(x, precision=None)` reproduces the pre-migration `op(x)` output BYTE-FOR-BYTE across a spread of x (incl. ±Inf, tiny, large, near-octant/quadrant boundaries), native AND numpy-absent pure — the reference literals captured from a pre-rename run.

**`precision=P` (int ≥ 1) → the EXACT-rational REFERENCE at `P` fractional bits.** Range-reduce `x` in EXACT rationals, call the matching `*_series_truncate` op with `num_terms` sized so the truncation remainder is < `2**-P`, recombine exactly, return a higher-precision exact `Q`. FLOAT-FREE in the value (the only float is the IEEE-754 read of the argument → its exact `as_integer_ratio`, and the discrete band/octant SELECTION). Per op: **exp** `x = n·ln2 + r`, `|r| ≤ ln2/2`, `exp_series` sized to `2**-(P+n₊)` then `× 2ⁿ` exact (a DERIVED exact ln2 = `−log1p(−1/2)`); **log** `x = m·2^e` bit-extracted, `log(m) = log1p(m−1)`, `|m−1| ≤ √2−1 ≈ 0.414` (~135 terms at P=160), `+ e·ln2` exact; **cos/sin** octant-reduce `|r| ≤ π/4` against a DERIVED exact π (`pi_cascade_digits`), Class-K ∘ Class-C octant sign (never `abs()`); **tan** = the exact `sin/cos` quotient; **atan** the exact THREE-BAND reduction (`|u| ≤ √2−1`), `atan(±Inf) = ±π/2`; **atan2** = `atan(y/x)` over the EXACT ratio + the same `±π` quadrant shift. **G2** asserts error < `2**-P` against an INDEPENDENT high-precision oracle (Python `decimal` with its own reduction — no numpy), the error SHRINKS with P, and the returned Q's denominator LENGTHENS with P (measured: at P=160, errors ~1e-55…1e-67, denominators 2k–12k bits). **G4** native == pure for `precision=P` (a Python reference path).

**`_classn_working(precision, kind="terms")` implemented** (the rc318 WAVE-1 `NotImplementedError` stub is replaced): `precision=None` → the fast/native Q61 regime marker (`mode="platform"`); `precision=P` → the SRMECH-NATIVE BIGINT regime whose `effective` is the fractional-bit budget `P`. Because each series has a different convergence rate, the ACTUAL per-op `num_terms` is computed by the new `_num_terms_for(bound, P, shape)` from the reduced-argument bound (pure-integer bit-length sizing, documented worst-case bound per op). `kind="den"` stays reserved.

**Raised series caps + native-cap gate (enabling machinery, byte-identical).** The `_TRIG_SERIES_MAX_TERMS` / `_LOG_SERIES_MAX_TERMS` guards rise 50/64 → **512** (matching `_EXP_SERIES_MAX_TERMS`) so the reference path can request enough terms for large P — a strict relaxation (every previously-accepted `num_terms` still validates; the bignum body has no ceiling). Because the C series arenas (`srmech_bigexp.c`) are sized for the old caps and reject a larger `num_terms` with `BAD_INPUT`, `_native._bigexp_call` now skips native above each op's `_BIGEXP_NATIVE_TERM_CAP` and lets the caller's ceilingless pure-Python bignum body compute the (byte-identical) partial sum. No C-side series change.

**No C signature change → ABI stays 10, `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 16, tool count UNCHANGED (492).** The Q61 C peers keep their signatures (only the Python wrapper keyword changed). The 9 `ToolEntry` parameter strings (`cos`/`sin`/`tan`/`atan`/`atan2`/`exp`/`log`/`cexp`/`complex_exp`: `terms` → `precision`) are updated; `srmech_tool_registry.c` regenerated to match (schema hash ratchet holds), `srmech_carrier_registry.c` + `_tool_docs.py` regenerated (idempotent — no count move). In-repo re-exporters (`trigonometry` / `calculus` / `asymptotic_calculus`) import the function objects and pick up the new signature automatically; no in-repo caller passed `terms=`. The WAVE-1 `_classn_working(kind="terms")` assertion is updated to the implemented behavior.

## [0.9.0rc314]

_**The CODON READ-LAYER — biology reads the genome in CODONS (triplets), and that reading is a PROCESS the ribosome IMPOSES over the stored strand, not stored substrate.** So rc314 adds a pure READ over the existing store: it stores nothing, changes no on-disk format (`GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 16), adds no carrier. `codon_read(strand, phase=0)` applies `q8_project_v4` FIRST (biology reads 4 BASES, not 8 signed states — the winding/center SIGN BIT must NOT leak into amino-acid identity), then slides a 3-slot window from the reading-frame offset `phase ∈ {0,1,2}`, forms a base-4 codon index `i = 16·b0 + 4·b1 + b2 ∈ [0,64)` over the 3 projected symbols (the 4 V₄ cosets labelled U/T, C, A, G in NCBI Base-order, so `i` IS the NCBI `transl_table=1` index), and a **Class-E** dense-catalog lookup `i → amino acid` against the ATTESTED Standard Genetic Code. `codon_frame_monodromy(strand)` reads the Z3 reading-frame monodromy of a CIRCULAR strand: going once around shifts the frame `φ → φ + L (mod 3)`, so it returns `L mod 3` — a REAL Z3 invariant (additive around laps; the frame CLOSES when `3 | L`)._

_**HONEST BOUNDING (three order-3 objects kept SEPARATE — do not conflate).** (a) the reading-frame phase `φ ∈ {0,1,2}` — a genuine cyclic **C3** (the ribosome's window), ADDED here; (b) `klein4_triality_cycle` — the base-axis order-3 automorphism (the S₃ generator relabelling the three non-identity cosets, already used for k=3 error-correction) — NOT the codon frame; (c) the winding `Lk` (rc309 center-parity; `cwf_consistency_mod2`) — lives in the Q₈ SIGN BIT, removed by `q8_project_v4` before any codon is read. There is NO codon copy of the integer `Lk`: the codon layer is frame topology in Z3, the winding lives in the sign bit. The read is FORM-not-identity — a stipulated labelling of the ribosome's read, not a claim about what the store means._

**ABI stays 10 — two ADDITIVE exported C symbols** (`srmech_genome_codon_read` + `srmech_genome_codon_frame_monodromy`), no exported-signature/struct/callback change, no new callback typedef. **`describe()["tools"]["total"]` moves 488 → 490** (`genome.codon_read` + `genome.codon_frame_monodromy`, category `genome`). **BOTH C registries regenerated** — `srmech_tool_registry.c` → 490 entries, `srmech_carrier_registry.c` reflows to carry the two new tool names in its sorted manifest (no carrier op added); `_tool_docs.py` (490 tools / 490 explanations / 490 examples) + `_c_claims.py` (the two new `srmech.amsc.genome.codon_*` claims) regenerated. `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 16 (a read changes no on-disk format). Rosetta: both `codon_read` and `codon_frame_monodromy` → `c_dispatched` (genome-fully-in-C: the wire-format ratchet requires a bare-C host to run every genome op, so each gets a whole-op C peer; no `non_compute` / four-way-split churn).

- **THE GENETIC-CODE TABLE — a REAL MPR-ATTESTED AMSC DATUM.** The 64 → 20(+stop) codon→amino-acid table ships as `srmech/amsc/attested/genetic_code/` (`descriptor.toml` + a full **MPR v1 envelope** `row.ndjson` + `row.schema.json`), a sibling to the other `attested/` catalogs — NEVER an inline invented dict (the fluent-domain-vocabulary failure mode: an invented table has no citation to check). Source: A. Elzanowski and J. Ostell, *The Genetic Codes* (NCBI; `gc.prt` / `Taxonomy/Utils/wprintgc.cgi`, `transl_table=1`); the `ncbieaa` amino-acid string was cross-verified **byte-identical** across the NCBI `wprintgc.cgi` page and the `gc.prt` data file. The standard code is public-domain biological fact (a U.S. Government / NCBI work). The mandatory `source_doi` is the peer-reviewed **OPEN-ACCESS** NCBI-Taxonomy resource paper (Schoch et al. 2020, *Database* (Oxford) 2020:baaa062, doi:`10.1093/database/baaa062`; PMC7408187) — an OA DOI, not a paywalled one. The full attestation block (all 9 mandatory fields) validates via `srmech.amsc.format.validate_mpr_record`, and `attestation.response_sha256 == sha256(data.source_response)` re-verifies over the committed source bytes (`ddda97af80cf929bcf22de86d80547e05da0f4eb24fa275e8869c51e63cb10d6`).
- **C (`srmech_genome.c` + decls in `srmech.h`).** `srmech_genome_codon_read` — projects each symbol (`& 3`) FIRST, slides the 3-slot window from `phase`, indexes the passed-in 64-byte `ncbieaa` table (attested data passed IN, never baked): Class-I (project + Z3 frame) ∘ Class-E (dense catalog). `srmech_genome_codon_frame_monodromy` — `n mod 3` (V₄ projection preserves length). _**The exact-rational DISCRETE WRITHE + the mod-2 Călugăreanu–White–Fuller check — the PHYSICAL-topology peer of the intrinsic mod-2 center-parity holonomy (`quaternion_cycle_holonomy`, rc309).** rc309 shipped the intrinsic `Lk` (the Q₈ cycle-holonomy center-parity — a mod-2 gauge-invariant integer). rc313 adds the physical topology: given a caller-supplied 3D embedding of the backbone (each vertex an EXACT RATIONAL, `int` / `Fraction` / `(num, den)` per coordinate), `discrete_writhe` computes `Wr` — the discrete Gauss double-sum over non-adjacent segment PAIRS in the z-drop projection: `Wr = Σ ε_ij`, `ε_ij = sign((B−A)·((D−C)×(C−A)))` when segments `i, j` cross in the xy-projection (four exact 2D orientation determinants decide the crossing), else `0`. No claim that DNA IS a quaternion, nor an integer-level CWF. No-embedding path returns ONLY the intrinsic mod-2 `Lk` (no `Wr` fabricated)._

## [0.9.0rc312]

_**GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION 15 → 16 — the on-disk migration for Q₈ (THE biggest break).** rc311 wired the Q₈ carrier into the genome as an `element_type` coupling path but the on-disk WIRE still assumed 2-bit klein4 turns, so a Q₈ (winding-bearing) genome could be coupled in RAM but not persisted. rc312 migrates the format so a Q₈ genome can be WRITTEN and READ from disk. The §55 packed-turn layer gains a SECOND codec: a Q₈ data turn 3-bit-packs under a new marker `Q8_PACKED_TURN_MARKER = 0x38` ('8', the 8-sector octet), where the klein4 turn 2-bit-packs under `PACKED_TURN_MARKER = 0x51` ('Q'). The new packing is MSB-FIRST CONTIGUOUS: symbol `i` occupies bits `[3i, 3i+3)` of a big-endian bitstream (symbol 0 in the highest bits, each 3-bit symbol's sign/high bit first), payload `ceil(leaf_dim*3/8)` bytes, the unused LOW bits of a partial final byte zero (canonical). The marker keys BOTH kind and width, so a v16 body is walked in the SAME self-describing scan (§44) as a v3 klein4 body — a reader strides each turn by its marker with NO element_type context. The manifest gains a `carrier` field ("klein4"/"q8"), derived from the body scan (the first packed turn's marker), so a loaded genome self-describes its element type. **klein4 keeps its 2-bit packer, so a klein4 body is BYTE-IDENTICAL to v15 — only the manifest `format_version` + `carrier` fields move.** A v15 klein4 turn (bytes 0..3, sign bit 0) IS the winding-0 slice of a v16 Q₈ turn (`q8_project_v4(turn) == turn`, every sign bit 0), so `upgrade_v15_to_v16` re-stamps a v15 genome to v16 with NO body repack._

**ABI stays 10 — the SSoT change is `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` (genome DATA format), NOT a C exported-signature/struct/callback wire change.** Per the project rule (ABI bumps only on an exported C FUNCTION signature/struct/callback change; the genome byte format is DATA), the v15→v16 bump does NOT move ABI. Two new **additive** exported C symbols — `srmech_genome_q8_pack_turn` / `srmech_genome_q8_unpack_turn` (the 3-bit codec primitives, genome-fully-in-C) — reuse NO callback typedef. **No new registered ToolEntry — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` STAYS 485** (`element_type` is a parameter on the existing `genome_save` callable; `upgrade_v15_to_v16` is an internal migration helper — the migrate-on-read/append precedent (v11→v12) — and the two Q₈ codec C peers are internal/parity-gate targets, not public callables). **BOTH C registries regenerate BYTE-IDENTICALLY** (`srmech_tool_registry.c` + `srmech_carrier_registry.c` — no tool_schema change); `_tool_docs.py` / `_c_claims.py` regenerate unchanged. New `upgrade_v15_to_v16(path, *, coupling=None)` re-derives the manifest from the unchanged body (klein4 needs no repack) and re-stamps v16 + carrier; idempotent. **Class-M** (bind) ∘ **Class-C** (the winding sign is a group-encoding BIT, **never** an `abs()`).

## [0.9.0rc310]

_The DISCRETE quaternion group `Q₈ = {±1,±i,±j,±k}` as 3-bit bytes — the discrete peer of the CONTINUOUS ℍ surface (`qm.quaternion`), and the safe foundation of the cascade-faithful Q8-genome arc. A byte `q∈{0..7}` is `q=(sign_bit<<2)|v4_coset` with `v4_coset=q&3∈{1,i,j,k}` and `sign_bit=q>>2∈{+,−}`, so `0=+1,1=+i,2=+j,3=+k,4=−1,…,7=−k`. The product is the cocycle of the central extension `1→Z₂→Q₈→V4→1`: `(s_a·e_{x_a})(s_b·e_{x_b}) = (s_a⊕s_b⊕F[x_a][x_b])·e_{x_a⊕x_b}`, where `F` is the sign bit of the Cayley–Dickson basis product (DERIVED from `cd_basis_product` at dim 4 — no hand-entered table). This is genuine Q₈: NON-abelian (`q8_mult(1,2)=3` but `q8_mult(2,1)=7`), `i²=j²=k²=4` (`−1`), associative over all 8×8×8. Pure INTEGER bit-arithmetic — no floats, so no FMA / FP-contraction concern. **ADDITIVE ONLY: no `genome.py` wiring, no `hdc.klein4_bind` change** — this rc ships the primitives + tests + ripple, nothing else moves._

No exported signature change, no callback typedef (uint8 ops carry no CFUNCTYPE wire implication). **Four new registered ToolEntries — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` moves 481 → 485** (`q8_mult`, `q8_conjugate`, `q8_bind`, `q8_project_v4`; category `q8`); **carriers stay 25; `CD_MAX_DIM` 256; `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 15** (no on-disk change — this is why the arc is safe to found here).

**THE LOAD-BEARING DIFFERENTIAL CONTRACT — the π: Q₈ → V4 homomorphism (measured, committed).** The abelian projection is EXACT: `(q8_mult(a,b) & 3) == ((a&3) ^ (b&3))` for **all** 64 `(a,b)` pairs — `V4 = q&3` is the F380/R21 homomorphism `π: Q₈ → V4 = Z₂×Z₂`, verified in `test_q8_carrier_rc310.py::test_pi_homomorphism_differential_contract`. It also agrees with the shipped abelian binder at the buffer level: `π(q8_bind(A,B)) == klein4_bind(π A, π B)` over the full 8×8 pair grid (`test_q8_projects_to_klein4_bind`). ## [0.9.0rc309]

_The NON-ABELIAN generalisation of `cycle_holonomy` (#944 follow-on) — the k=2 discrete which-way / **Lk-analog** channel over the quaternion units `Q₈ = {±1,±i,±j,±k}`. Where the abelian `laplacian.cycle_holonomy` reads a fundamental cycle's net charge (a rational in turns, mod 1), `qm.quaternion.quaternion_cycle_holonomy` reads the ordered **quaternion product** walked around the cycle, `H = P_u·g_uv·conj(P_v)` (`P_x` = the tree-path root→x product; a reversed edge contributes `conj(gain)` = its inverse). A node-wise re-gauge `g_uv→s_u·g_uv·conj(s_v)` telescopes to `H→s_root·H·conj(s_root)`: the holonomy is CONJUGATED by the base-point gauge, so its **conjugacy class is gauge-invariant** — the non-abelian form of Zaslavsky's switching theory. The frame-free read is the **SU(2) conjugacy class = the scalar part `w=Re(H)`** (a conjugation invariant: `Re(s·H·conj(s))=Re(H)`): for a Q₈-derived connection `w∈{+1,0,−1}`, giving three classes `0={1}`, `1={−1}` (the spinor / Lk half-twist), `2={±i,±j,±k}` (pure-imaginary)._

**No ABI change — ABI stays 10.** Three new **additive** C symbols — `srmech_quaternion_conjugate` (the unit inverse; `quaternion_conjugate` now native-dispatched, so its Rosetta bucket flips `composition_of_c → c_dispatched`), plus `srmech_quaternion_cycle_holonomy` + `srmech_quaternion_cycle_holonomy_arena_bytes` (the non-abelian generalisation of `srmech_graph_cycle_holonomy`, reusing the union-find spanning-forest scaffolding; `ws_len` guarded in **BYTES** per the rc307 discipline). No exported signature change, no callback typedef. **One new registered ToolEntry — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` moves 480 → 481** (`quaternion_cycle_holonomy`; `quaternion_conjugate` already counted); **carriers stay 25; `CD_MAX_DIM` 256; `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 15** (no on-disk change).

**THE PROOF GATE — re-gauge invariance (measured, committed).** Only the *conjugacy class* of a non-abelian cycle product is gauge-invariant, so it was MEASURED, not assumed (`test_quaternion_cycle_holonomy_rc309.py::test_regauge_invariance_proof_gate`): across the triangle / theta-digon / K₄ / 5-cycle, over many random re-gauge draws, the per-cycle **SU(2) `class_index` is UNCHANGED** to ~1e-15 while the **raw holonomy quaternion genuinely MOVES** (different Q₈ element / rotated axis). The finding worth stating: the finer 5-class Q₈ split `{±i}`/`{±j}`/`{±k}` is invariant only under **discrete Q₈** re-gauge; under **continuous** unit-quaternion re-gauge SU(2) merges the three imaginary axes (`i` and `j` are SU(2)-conjugate), so the frame-free keystone is the **scalar-part (SU(2)) class**, which the op ships as `class_index` — the sound "Lk = conjugacy class" reading. `center_parity` (the `{1}`/`{−1}` central sign) is a class function, hence also invariant.

- **`qm/quaternion.py`.** `quaternion_cycle_holonomy(edges, gains=None, *, n=None) -> dict` (**Class M** quaternion bind ∘ **Class L** graph ∘ **Class C** orientation; sign is **Class K + Class C**, never `abs()`) returning `{'n_cycles', 'class_index', 'center_parity', 'cycle_edges', 'holonomies' (raw ℍ), 'balanced'}`; native standalone-C dispatch (`has_native_quaternion_cycle_holonomy`) with a byte-exact pure-Python cascade fallback (the quaternion product built from the exact `±a_i` structure table, so native == pure to the bit). `quaternion_conjugate` gains native dispatch (`srmech_quaternion_conjugate`). `quaternion_cycle_holonomy` added to `__all__`.
- **C.** `srmech_quaternion_conjugate` in `srmech_quaternion.c`; `srmech_quaternion_cycle_holonomy` + `_arena_bytes` in `srmech_laplacian.c` (JPL-clean: caller-arena, no malloc, ≤60-line functions, ≥2 asserts each, no goto; the quaternion product reuses the exported `srmech_quaternion_left_mult` so the Cayley-Dickson convention has ONE source of truth). `_native.py` binds all three (hasattr-guarded, ABI stays 10) + `has_native_quaternion_cycle_holonomy()`.
- **Ripple.** +1 `ToolEntry` (category `qm.quaternion`); `_tool_docs.py` regenerated (481 tools/explanations/examples); `rosetta_classification.ndjson` — `quaternion_conjugate` flipped to `c_dispatched`, +1 `quaternion_cycle_holonomy`→`c_dispatched` row; `_c_claims.py` regenerated (the two ops resolve to their new C symbols against the loaded lib); BOTH C registries regenerated (`srmech_tool_registry.c` + `srmech_carrier_registry.c`) so the byte-identity ratchets hold; the 56 `describe()["tools"]["total"]` count-test pins bumped 480 → 481.
- **CITATIONS (DERIVED, not attested-new).** The gain-graph switching / cycle-gain framing is T. Zaslavsky, "Signed graphs", Discrete Appl. Math. 4 (1982) 47–74 (the non-abelian conjugacy-class read is the group-valued generalisation); the ℍ / Q₈ gain algebra is the octonion module's Cayley–Dickson convention at dim 4 (Baez, J.C. (2002) *The Octonions*, arXiv:math/0105155, §1). No new attested datum.
- **Tests (`test_quaternion_cycle_holonomy_rc309.py`, numpy-free).** The re-gauge-invariance proof gate (above); native == pure byte-for-byte parity across all four graphs and random Q₈ + continuous re-gauges; holonomy on known cycles (a triangle with a known Q₈ product → the correct class); `quaternion_conjugate` correctness + native dispatch; the balanced-graph (identity gains) control; the class/center_parity semantics; error/edge cases; the registration ratchet. The JPL Power-of-Ten ratchet stays green.

## [0.9.0rc308]

_The ℍ (associative) sibling of `magnetic_laplacian` (#944). `magnetic_laplacian` is the ℂ (dim-2) complex-unit-gain Laplacian (Reff 2012); `quaternion_laplacian` is its dim-4 ASSOCIATIVE rung — a 4n×4n REAL-SYMMETRIC matrix whose (u,v) block is the 4×4 real left-multiplication rep `L(g)` of a unit-quaternion gain `g∈Sp(1)`, (v,u) block `L(conj g)=L(g)ᵀ` (symmetric BY CONSTRUCTION), diagonal block `(Σ w/2)·I₄`. It carries two spectral facts the ℂ leg cannot: the spectrum is GAUGE-INVARIANT under the node-wise unit-quaternion gauge `g_uv→s_u·g_uv·conj(s_v)` (~3.3e-15; the ℍ generalisation of the U(1) gauge invariance), and every eigenvalue is ×4 DEGENERATE — a THEOREM, since ℍ associativity makes the left-built matrix commute with the fixed right-ℍ Sp(1) commutant, so callers dedupe every 4th. `hypercomplex_perspectives` is the scalar/imaginary channel reader (`4 = 1 + 3` for ℍ) that ALSO closes the latent dim-2 read of `magnetic_laplacian` (`2 = 1 + 1` for ℂ), serving ℝ/ℂ/ℍ by `dim`._

**No ABI change — ABI stays 10.** Both ops are pure-Python **Class-L compositions over already-C-backed atoms** (`quaternion_left_mult`→`srmech_quaternion_left_mult`, `mat_hermitian_eigendecompose`→`srmech_hermitian_eigendecompose_ws`) — no exported signature change, no new C symbol, no callback typedef. Honest C parity holds today: a bare-C host assembles both matrices and eigendecomposes them. **Two new registered ToolEntries — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` moves 478 → 480** (`quaternion_laplacian` + `hypercomplex_perspectives`); **carriers stay 25; `CD_MAX_DIM` 256; `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` 10; `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 15** (no on-disk change).

- **`laplacian.py`.** `quaternion_laplacian(n, edges, weights=None, *, gains=None) -> Mat` (**Class L** composing the **Class-M** `quaternion_left_mult` bind; gain conjugate is **Class C** via `quaternion_conjugate`; gain normalisation to Sp(1) is **Class K + Class C** via `quaternion_norm` — an exact-rational 4-vector hypot, never an ALU `abs()`) + `hypercomplex_perspectives(eigvecs, dim=4) -> dict` (**Class L** spectral read-out; a pure structural split). `gains=None` collapses to the undirected control `½·(dense Laplacian) ⊗ I₄`. Both names added to `__all__` (top list + `LAPLACIAN_OPS`).
- **Ripple.** +2 `ToolEntry` in `tool_schema.py` (category `laplacian`, canonical-cited summaries); `_tool_docs.py` regenerated (480 tools, 480 explanations, 480 examples); +2 `rosetta_classification.ndjson` rows (`quaternion_laplacian`→`composition_of_c`, `hypercomplex_perspectives`→`non_compute`/`composes_c`); the C tool registry (`c/src/srmech_tool_registry.c`) regenerated so its byte-identity + `tool_schema_sha256` ratchet holds; the 56 `describe()["tools"]["total"] == 478` count-test pins bumped to 480.
- **CITATIONS (DERIVED, not attested-new).** The complex-unit-gain spectral framing generalises one Cayley–Dickson rung: N. Reff, "Spectral Properties of Complex Unit Gain Graphs", Linear Algebra Appl. 436 (2012) 3165–3176 (arXiv:1110.4554); the ℍ gain algebra is the octonion module's Cayley–Dickson convention at dim 4 (Baez, J.C. (2002) *The Octonions*, arXiv:math/0105155, §1). No new attested datum.
- **Tests (`test_quaternion_laplacian_rc308.py`, 21 checks, numpy-free).** Shape + EXACT real-symmetry (`L(conj g) == L(g)ᵀ` term-by-term); gauge-invariance (<1e-11, measured ~1.8e-15); the ×4 degeneracy theorem (n distinct quadruples); the identity-gain `½·(dense L) ⊗ I₄` known answer; native == pure parity of the assembled matrix (monkeypatched `HAS_NATIVE`); the dim-2 (ℂ) and dim-4 (ℍ) channel splits (synthetic known-answers + end-to-end on both Laplacians); error/edge cases; the registration ratchet.

## [0.9.0rc307]

_The `fiedler_sparse` family's `ws_len` unit is UNIFIED to the house BYTES convention (§51 / task #903). `srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse` / `_file` / `_file_progress` guarded `ws_len` as a **COUNT OF DOUBLES** (`ws_len < 8u*n`) while the rest of the caller-arena laplacian surface — `k_extreme_modes_file`, `recursive_cut`, and every `*_arena_bytes` peer — counts **BYTES**. That three-way split was fail-safe IN-TREE only because the Python sizer happened to over-size; the real hazard is an EXTERNAL bare-C host sizing a `ws` buffer by the wrong convention against one confusingly-mixed surface._

**ABI 9 → 10 — a breaking wire-CONTRACT change (the `ws_len` UNIT of three existing exported functions is reinterpreted; not a callback typedef, not a removal).** New C symbol `srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse_arena_bytes(n)` = `8*n*sizeof(double)` (mirrors the other `*_arena_bytes` helpers); the three fiedler guards flip from `ws_len < 8u*n` to `ws_len < srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse_arena_bytes(n)`, so `ws_len` is BYTES uniformly across the whole laplacian surface. A caller passing the OLD doubles count now under-sizes the arena 8× and is correctly declined (`SRMECH_ERR_BAD_INPUT`) rather than silently reading OOB — the ABI bump is what tells an out-of-tree caller to re-read the contract. **No new op — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 478** (the `*_arena_bytes` helper is C-internal, NOT a registered ToolEntry); **carriers stay 25; `CD_MAX_DIM` 256; `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` 10; `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 15** (no on-disk change).

- **THE INTERNAL-CALLER CATCH (the one an 8× under-size would silently corrupt).** `recursive_cut`'s `rcut_bisect` calls `srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse_file` INTERNALLY, and it was passing `(size_t)8u * count` — a DOUBLES count. Left unchanged under the flipped BYTES guard, that site would under-size the Fiedler workspace 8× and `recursive_cut` would corrupt/decline on every non-trivial graph. It is updated in lockstep to `srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse_arena_bytes(count)`. `s->ws` spans exactly `8n` doubles up to `s->fv`, so for `count ≤ n` the arena is still sufficient — only the SIZE ARGUMENT'S UNIT had to change. Grepped every internal caller of the fiedler family: this (`srmech_laplacian.c:2349`) is the ONLY one in `c/src/` (`spectral_spine.c` names it in a comment, does not call it).
- **BOTH projections change in lockstep.** `EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION` 9 → 10; the three Python ctypes dispatch sites (`laplacian.py` `_fiedler_sparse_native` / `_fiedler_sparse_file_native`, `_native.py` `fiedler_sparse_file_native_progress`) now pass `ctypes.sizeof(ws)` (BYTES) instead of the doubles count. The pure-Python bodies are UNTOUCHED, so native == pure holds. All 20 ABI pins across the test suite updated 9 → 10.
- **The header docs** for the three functions now state `ws_len` is BYTES from `srmech_laplacian_fiedler_sparse_arena_bytes(n)`; the `recursive_cut` doc's "note: BYTES, unlike the fiedler_sparse family's DOUBLES" is corrected (the odd-one-out is gone). The v10 ABI-progression note is added to both `srmech.h` and `_native.py`.
- **The `c_claims` manifest** is regenerated (only the ABI number in its docstring moves 9 → 10 — the fiedler dispatch path names no new symbol, since the Python side sizes via `ctypes.sizeof` rather than calling the helper). The tool/carrier/class/responsion registries and `tool_schema_sha256` are UNCHANGED.
- **Tests.** The two C smokes (`test_srmech_fiedler.c`, `test_srmech_fiedler_file.c`) move to the BYTES convention and each gains a "the OLD doubles-count (`8*n`) is now an 8× under-size → `BAD_INPUT`" assertion (which distinguishes the new guard from the old: `8*6=48 < arena_bytes(6)=384`) plus a "`ws_len < arena_bytes(n)` → `BAD_INPUT`" guard-rejection at the exact new threshold. The existing `test_native_matches_pure` (fiedler_sparse / _file) and `test_recursive_cut_parity_rc284` prove native == pure post-change AND that `recursive_cut` still partitions real graphs (it would corrupt/decline if the `:2349` site were left as a doubles count).

## [0.9.0rc306]

_`srmech_genome_section_counts` becomes CALLER-ARENA (§102 / task #899). The op that re-derives `{global_id: n_sections}` from a plasmid store scanned against THREE file-scope static scratch buffers — a 32 MiB catalog arena, a 2^18-slot count table, a 64 KiB window (+ a static id counter). That made it BOTH corpus-capped (`srmech_genome_arena_bytes`'s ~2.7 KiB/chromosome term filled the 32 MiB arena at **~11,000 sections**, past which a native scan silently declined to the pure body) AND **non-reentrant** — an exception to the reentrant-C-core claim (#772) and a real hazard for a threaded host embedding `libsrmech`._

**ABI 8 → 9 — the first ORDINARY-kind bump (an existing exported signature changed, not a callback typedef, not a removal).** `srmech_genome_section_counts` gains `(void *ws, size_t ws_len)`; the count table + region window are carved off the caller `ws` and the untouched TAIL is the catalog arena `genome_obtain_manifest` parses into — the exact caller-arena route the JSON/TOML parsers (rc159/rc160) and the CD dimension (`#933`) already use. No static scan state remains: the op is **reentrant** on disjoint `ws` buffers, and the corpus bound is whatever `ws` the caller sizes. **No new op — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 478; carriers stay 25; `CD_MAX_DIM` 256; `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` 10; `GENOME_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 15** (no on-disk change — the counts stay byte-identical to the pure body).

- **The sizing helper.** New C symbol `srmech_genome_section_counts_arena_bytes(body_len, n_chroms, out_cap)` (mirroring the other `*_arena_bytes` helpers): catalog term = `srmech_genome_arena_bytes(body_len, n_chroms, 0)` (scales with the corpus), count table sized to hold `out_cap` distinct ids under the 3/4 open-addressing load bound (floored so a tiny store still gets headroom), + a 64 KiB window + alignment slop. It is a pure-integer helper, NOT a registered ToolEntry (so `tools.total` is unchanged).
- **BOTH projections change in lockstep.** The Python `_native.py` ctypes binding gains the `ws`/`ws_len` params; `EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION` 8 → 9; `genome_section_counts_c` now sizes `ws` via the helper (from `body_len` = turns.bin bytes and `n_chroms` = the manifest chromosome count `plasmid.section_counts` already has) and grows `ws` + the out arrays together on overflow (exact retry when the table held the ids and only the out arrays were short; geometric otherwise), so a corpus with any number of distinct ids — past the old 196,608-id ceiling — censuses natively given memory. The **pure Python body is UNTOUCHED**, so C-vs-Python parity holds (native == pure, byte-for-byte).
- **The count table's 2^18 ceiling is gone too.** Because the table is sized from `out_cap` (which the retry loop grows) rather than a compile-time constant.
- **The `c_claims` manifest updates** (regenerated): `srmech.amsc.plasmid.section_counts` now claims BOTH `srmech_genome_section_counts` and `srmech_genome_section_counts_arena_bytes`. The tool/carrier/class/responsion registries and `tool_schema_sha256` are UNCHANGED (no ToolEntry moved).
- **Tests.** New `test_plasmid_section_counts_arena_rc306.py` proves: the sizing helper scales past the old 32 MiB static (so past the ~11k cap) and past the 196,608-id ceiling; the three statics + two cap macros are gone from the C source (the reentrancy proof); native == pure across small AND larger fixtures; and the caller-arena retry-grow engages (and stays correct) when the initial capacity is forced tiny. The rc280 C smoke (`test_srmech_genome.c`, 196 asserts) and the rc280 pytest (18) pass unchanged against the new signature. All 16 ABI pins updated 8 → 9.

## [0.9.0rc305]

_Rebased onto rc304 (which added `genome_from_graph`'s `attestation=` parameter); this rc extends the SAME op's ToolEntry additively with `composes`/`preserves`, and the generated tool registry is regenerated against the rc304 genome_from_graph so the byte-identity ratchet holds._

**Two deliverables in one rc: (A) `ToolEntry.composes` / `.preserves` — the Siona compose-a-cascade CAPSTONE (`#943`); (B) the `test_bus_aio` discovery-cleanup flake FIXED AT ROOT (`#920`), not worked around.** **No new op — `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays 478; no new C symbol — ABI stays 8; carriers stay 25, `CD_MAX_DIM` 256, `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` 10.** The `c_claims` manifest is unchanged. The **`tool_schema_sha256` DOES move** (two new keys ride every composite ToolEntry's canonical JSON) — the C serialiser mirrors in lockstep so the byte-identity + hash ratchets recompute clean.

### `#943` — `composes` / `preserves`: a cascade is CROSS-OP, and now it is DATA

- **The gap.** `describe()` / `example` are PER-OP; the knowledge to CHAIN ops — "op A feeds op B, preserving invariant X" — lived only in CHANGELOG prose Siona cannot read as data. rc305 adds two STRUCTURED fields to every `ToolEntry`: **`composes`** (the ordered sub-ops an op is built from; empty for a leaf — the correct default) and **`preserves`** (the invariants it maintains).
- **Claims that are TRUE — the exact defect class this rc line corrects.** A populated `composes` can never name a phantom op: `test_composes_preserves_rc305.py` sweeps the WHOLE registry and fails if any `composes` entry is not a real registered tool or any `preserves` entry is blank. The F1299 worked example, `genome_from_graph`, is pinned to its TRACED cascade `[genome_partition → graph_to_kernel → mint_strand → genome_save → genome_census]` (read off `genome.py`, call-order), with the byte-exact `kernel_to_graph` round-trip stated in `preserves`.
- **Coverage, stated honestly.** Only `genome_from_graph` carries composition data this rc — it is the one cascade traced end-to-end against its implementation. Every other op keeps the empty-tuple leaf default (NOT fabricated composition). The field is the vehicle; population grows op-by-op as each cascade is traced, under the whole-registry claim-is-true gate.
- **The data rides the curation floor** (`_tool_docs_curated.py` → `gen_tool_docs.py` → `_tool_docs.py` → `_apply_docs`), the SAME path `explanation`/`example` already use, so a hand-written registration literal still wins and the un-rederivable-prose guard stays satisfied.
- **THE C-SERIALISER MIRROR (the ripple most agents miss).** The tool registry is rebuilt field-by-field in C (`srmech_tool_schema.c`) and the C-vs-Python byte-identity + `tool_schema_sha256` hash-ratchet compare against it. Adding two emitted keys means the C side MUST emit them too: `srmech_tool_entry_t` grew `composes`/`preserves` string-array fields (APPEND-only struct growth → ABI stays 8; the ctypes mirror reads only the field prefix, unchanged), `gen_tool_registry.py` bakes the per-entry arrays, and `ts_emit_entry` emits `"composes"` (sorted between `category` and `example`) + `"preserves"` (between `parameters` and `returns`). Verified BYTE-IDENTICAL: C JSON == Python SSoT (679459 bytes), `sha256(C) == tool_schema_sha256`.

### `#920` — the `test_bus_aio` flake, fixed at its ROOT (the readiness-race diagnosis was refuted by the code)

- **REPRODUCED first, and the first diagnosis did NOT hold.** The suspected cause — `_wait_for_endpoint` trusting an `alive` flag that flips true before the server accepts — is refuted by the code: `by_name().alive` already verifies via a real connect-probe (`_endpoint_alive_uds`), so the helper already waits for genuine acceptance. 640+ hammered iterations (unloaded, under 8 CPU burners, and the full bus family under `--dist load`) never reproduced a send-timeout. The ACTUAL root cause is the one the rc283 conftest workaround's own CHANGELOG note recorded: **`list_endpoints(cleanup_dead=True)` DELETES any socket whose 50 ms connect-probe fails — but a server inside its `bind()`→`listen()` window, or one whose accept backlog is momentarily full, refuses/times-out that probe IDENTICALLY to a crashed server's stale file.** Under a shared `~/.srmech/` (xdist workers share HOME) one worker's routine discovery sweep therefore unlinks another worker's IN-FLIGHT socket, surfacing as `FileNotFoundError: no bus endpoint` or `BusError: reader exited; peer closed`. Reproduced DETERMINISTICALLY: a bound-not-listening socket AND a backlog-full listening socket are both judged dead and unlinked by a sweep.
- **Root fix — cleanup now CONFIRMS death before unlinking.** A pathname-bound UDS socket appears in `/proc/net/unix` the instant `bind()` returns, independent of `listen()`/`accept()` — the liveness signal the connect-probe structurally cannot provide. `list_endpoints` takes one `/proc/net/unix` snapshot per sweep and unlinks a dead-LOOKING UDS registration ONLY when it is confirmed absent there (truly orphaned). Where the proof is unavailable (macOS/BSD — no `/proc/net/unix`) cleanup DECLINES to delete, since a mis-deletion corrupts a live peer while a genuinely-stale file self-heals at the next `bind()`. `alive` reporting is unchanged; only the destructive decision is narrowed. Genuine cleanup is preserved — an orphaned file with no live owner is still removed (verified). The rc283 conftest HOME-isolation STAYS as defence-in-depth (it also carries the macOS `sun_path` cap fix); this makes the LIBRARY correct so the workaround is no longer load-bearing.
- **Proof the flake is dead:** `test_bus_discovery_cleanup_rc305.py` — a bound-not-listening socket and a backlog-full socket each SURVIVE a sweep, a real accepting endpoint survives 25 concurrent sweeps, and an orphaned file is still cleaned; each survive-assertion was made to fail once (fix defeated) before trusting it. The whole `test_bus_aio.py` family runs clean under `-n auto`.

## [0.9.0rc304]

**A corpus genome can now attest its OWN source. `genome_from_graph` / `genome_save` take a caller `attestation=` whose fields OVERRIDE the srmech-default MPR written into `manifest.json`, so an attested corpus genome (e.g. a simplewiki dump whose true source is `https://dumps.wikimedia.org/simplewiki/latest/` under CC-BY-SA-4.0) records its REAL provenance instead of misattributing itself to `srmech.net/genome/persistence` / `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`.** This is an MPM integrity fix, not cosmetics: the genome directory is the SSoT with NO sidecar files (§41/F1300), so the manifest is the ONLY legitimate home for a genome's source attestation — before rc304 `no-sidecar` and `MPR-provenance` were in direct conflict, and a real corpus genome asserted a false source, exactly the citation-drift the AMSC attestation block exists to prevent. **No new op, no new C symbol; ABI stays 8.** `describe()["tools"]["total"]` stays **478** (only `genome_from_graph`'s ToolEntry gains a parameter); carriers stay **25**, `CD_MAX_DIM` stays **256**, `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` stays **10**, and the `c_claims` manifest is unchanged.

### §113 / `#1466` (task `#942`) — a caller-supplied genome source attestation

- **`genome_from_graph(…, attestation=)` and `genome_save(…, attestation=)`** — a caller MPR source-attestation whose provided fields override the srmech default in `manifest.json`. Threaded `genome_from_graph → genome_save → _manifest_record`; `graph_to_kernel` only builds the strand (it writes no manifest) and is untouched.
- **OVERRIDE-ONLY, restricted to the five SOURCE-identity fields** (`source_doi` / `source_url` / `license` / `retrieved_at` / `response_sha256`). A provided field replaces its default; an absent field keeps its default (a partial dict never blanks the rest — a caller supplying `source_url` + `license` keeps srmech's other fields). The four ENCODER-identity fields (`parser_version` / `parser_rule_hash` / `collector_descriptor_path` / `collector_descriptor_hash`) stay srmech-owned, so a caller attests the corpus source WITHOUT being able to misreport which srmech version / rule wrote the bytes. Overriding `response_sha256` (an MPR's response = the corpus dump) is SAFE: genome body integrity is anchored on the separate `data["body_sha256"]` (re-hashed on `genome_load`), NOT on `attestation.response_sha256`, so a dump-sha override cannot weaken integrity (proven).
- **A bad override is REJECTED before any bytes hit disk** — a non-dict (`TypeError`), an unknown / disallowed key (`ValueError`, incl. a typo'd `source_uri` or an attempt to overwrite an encoder field — the very misattribution the parameter prevents), or a value that makes the merged block an invalid MPR (`MPRValidationError` via `srmech.amsc.format.validate_mpr_record`). Never written silently.
- **Multi-implementation parity (ADR-0009 / the capability is the invariant).** The native `srmech_genome_save` writes the srmech DEFAULT MPR and takes no override, so the override is applied by the PURE manifest write (the already-materialised `body_bytes` + the overridden head-only manifest). PROVEN byte-identical across projections: the native-default and pure-default manifests are byte-for-byte equal, and an override manifest is byte-for-byte equal whether native is present or not; `turns.bin` is byte-identical with or without an attestation (the override touches ONLY the manifest). The default save is byte-identical to rc303 (modulo the version string). **C conclusion:** the bare-C `srmech_genome_save` entry still writes the default — minting a custom source attestation from a pure-C host (an additive `srmech_genome_save_attested` symbol; ABI-neutral) is a tracked follow-up, deliberately deferred to keep this rc's `c_claims` / ABI / registry surface unchanged.
- **Proof:** `tests/test_genome_attestation_rc304.py` (19 tests — round-trip, disk-persist, MPR-validate, census read-back, response_sha256-integrity, override-only partial, native≡pure parity, five rejection cases). Ripple: `_tool_docs.py` settled FIRST (example re-derives with the new param; `--accept-seed-drift` for the signature change, the curated explanation survives), then `srmech_tool_registry.c` regenerated (param count 10→11); the other three C registries byte-identical; generated in WSL, CRLF-restored; `.so` rebuilt before any test.

## [0.9.0rc303]

**The df-gated ABOUTNESS grounding encoder ships as the first RBS-LM op in the LLM-facing `tool_schema` — "which srmech op does this utterance want?" is now one call (`srmech.rbs_lm.encode_aboutness`), grounding at 72% top-1 over the tool_schema where the shipped `encode_sentence_l3` floors at 17%.** The F1008 (SIONA-INFER-2, `research/rbs-lm-rolling-2` PR #687) recipe promoted from research to a packaged capability, on the STRUCTURE-BEARING side of the F1260 axis. **No new C symbol; ABI stays 8.** `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **477 → 478** (one op); carriers stay **25**, `CD_MAX_DIM` stays **256**, `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` stays **10**, the `non_compute` split is untouched, and the `c_claims` manifest is unchanged.

### §112 / `#1462` (task `#941`) — the df-gated grounding encoder

- **Premise VERIFIED by measurement, not trusted.** The tracker claimed `encode_sentence_l3` grounds at the ~1/5 orthogonality floor "because it rides seed-based `encode_word_k4`". Measured over the shipped `tool_schema` on the 18-utterance F1008 eval: the shipped encoder grounds at **top-1 3/18 = 17%** in BOTH modes — `byteglyph` (the default, NOT the seed path) *and* `wordhash`. So the floor is real but the named mechanism is imprecise: the cause is the MISSING doc-frequency gate / name-weighting / order-aware bigrams, not the token backend. Generating code + NDJSON: `docs/srmech/notes/rc303_df_grounding_measurement.py` (+ `.ndjson`).
- **`srmech.rbs_lm.encode_aboutness(text, *, D, df=, n_docs=, name=, token_mode=…)`** — the F1008 recipe as one op: (1) a **doc-frequency aboutness GATE** (F768/F984 — drop catalog-wide function words), (2) **NAME-weighting** (F769 — an op's own name tokens count 3× unigram + 2× bigram), (3) **order-aware BIGRAMS** (`[[feedback_never_bag_of_words]]` — `(klein,4)` ≠ `(klein,gordon)`), plus letter-digit tokenization (`klein4`→`klein 4`). **Measured HERE: top-1 13/18 = 72.2%, top-3 77.8%** over the tool_schema — the number from THIS repo's committed generating code, not a quoted figure. It is lower than the research branch's F1008 **78%** (over 347 tools) for a mundane, non-regression reason: this eval is n=18 and one of its targets, `klein4_random`, was **removed from the schema in rc292**, so it is an automatic miss for every encoder (13/17 = 76% on the resolvable targets). Report is the reproduced 72.2%, honestly, over the committed NDJSON. Companion one-call surface `ground_tool_schema(utterance)` fits the gate over the live catalog and returns the top-k tools.
- **Structure-bearing, NOT high-diffusion (F1260).** Grounding is a REPRESENTATION problem, so tokens are minted via the COMPOSED `klein4_encode_bytes` (default `token_mode="byteglyph"`), NOT the high-diffusion word-hash `klein4_address` — a SHA avalanche makes a good ADDRESS but destroys morphology (F1260). The discriminant holds: `cat`/`cats` = **0.66** while `cat`/`dog` = **0.25** (byteglyph); the offered `token_mode="address"` dual floors BOTH (0.26 / 0.25) and is documented as NOT structure-bearing. The tradeoff is honest and small: byteglyph MATCHES the address recipe on **top-1 (both 72%)** at a modest **top-3** cost (78% vs the address dual's 89%) — the morphological similarity byteglyph adds is exactly what passes F1260 and it costs nothing at top-1, where grounding actually decides.
- **Classification honesty (`composition_of_c`, no C symbol).** The representation-bearing compute is a transitive composition of `c_dispatched` Klein-4 primitives (`klein4_encode_bytes` → `bind`/`bundle`/`random`); the tokenizer / gate / name-weighting are Python SELECTION glue over which C-backed atoms compose — exactly the existing rbs_lm ladder. There is NO dedicated `srmech_rbs_lm_encode_aboutness` symbol, so this is NOT `c_dispatched` — the honest narrow bucket is `composition_of_c` (both `encode_aboutness` and `ground_tool_schema`; the tokenizer + df-counter stay PRIVATE so the ledger never has to account for a bare tokenizer as a compute op). Rosetta: two `composition_of_c` rows; all four debt ceilings stay 0.
- **Ripple gate applied in order.** `_tool_docs.py` settled FIRST (+1 line, executed example, no refusal), then all four generated C registries: **`tool` moved (+the op) and `carrier` renumbered** (the auto-derived carrier back-index picks up the op's HV references — a legitimate transitive ripple, confirmed idempotent), **`class`/`responsion` byte-identical**; generated in WSL and CRLF-restored. `.so` rebuilt before any test. `describe()["tools"]["total"]` 477 → 478 across **56 assertions in 50 modules in seven literal forms**.

## [0.9.0rc302]

**The Class-I modular family is now DSL-DECLARABLE and DISCOVERABLE — a modular-arithmetic cascade (an LCG, a hash, the PCG64 step) can be composed as a TOML chain, not only hand-written in Python.** Before rc302 only `cyclic_gcd` lived in the cascade catalog, so a modular cascade could not be declared via `srmech.dsl.chain` / `make_class` at all. **No new C symbol; ABI stays 8.** `describe()["tools"]["total"]` **470 → 477**; carriers stay **25**, `CD_MAX_DIM` stays **256**, `CEIL_WIRE_GLUE_GAPS` stays **10**, the `non_compute` split is untouched. The `c_claims` manifest gains exactly one entry (`cyclic.bigint_mul` → `srmech_bigint_mul`); all other new ops are `composition_of_c`.

### §110 / `#1460` — chain-register the Class-I modular family + a 128-bit-capable modular multiply

- **The modular family becomes cascade ops (5 new catalog TOMLs).** `cyclic_mod_mul` / `cyclic_mod_add` / `cyclic_mod_pow` / `cyclic_mod_inv` join the cascade catalog as thin delegations to the already-`c_dispatched` `srmech.amsc.cyclic.*` primitives (`composition_of_c`; no native dispatch of their own). Following the DSL chain contract the piped value is the first positional arg and the operands are bound stage kwargs, so an LCG step reads `chain().then("cyclic_mod_mul", b=MULT, n=MOD).then("cyclic_mod_add", b=INC, n=MOD)` — proven to match hand-composed Python over the catalog list-op count **15 → 20**.
- **`cyclic.mod_mul_wide(a, b, n)` — the uncapped modular multiply.** `mod_mul` stays correctly capped at uint64 (it binds the fixed-64-bit ABI `srmech_mod_mul`); `mod_mul_wide` is the separate uncapped companion (chosen over a `bits=` param so the capped guard is never weakened). It routes the product through srmech's own C bignum `srmech_bigint_mul` (via the new `cyclic.bigint_mul`) and reduces mod `n`, so the raw PCG64 128-bit LCG step (`n = 2**128`, multiplier `0x2360ed051fc65da44385df649fccf645`) is expressible where the capped op cannot. `composition_of_c` — packaging an existing capability, not a new one. Also a cascade op (`cyclic_mod_mul_wide`).

### §112 / `#1462` — register the bignum multiply + give summaries user-facing aboutness

- **`cyclic.bigint_mul` + `cyclic.mod_mul_wide` join the public `tool_schema`.** The bignum multiply (previously only `_native.bigint_mul_c`) is now a discoverable, always-correct public op so Siona can recommend the op a wide modular cascade relies on. `cyclic.bigint_mul` is `c_dispatched` (`srmech_bigint_mul`); the 5 cascade ops + `mod_mul_wide` are registered too (7 new ToolEntries total).
- **Aboutness clauses added (implementation words kept).** `cyclic.mod_mul` now leads with "Modular multiply — (a * b) mod n" (keeping "russian-peasant doubling"); `cyclic.mod_pow` leads with "Modular exponentiation" (keeping "square-and-multiply"); `cascade.magnitude` now says "Absolute value |x|" (keeping "Class K pin-slot at zero"). A caller searching "modular multiply" / "absolute value" now hits the tool.

## [0.9.0rc301]
